resource_contract.architecture: Shared DreamCo infrastructure with isolated per-division namespaces, model identities, dataset lanes, authorization scopes, metrics, and rollback pointers.
resource_contract.model_strategy: Start with shared, license-reviewed base models plus division-specific adapters or compact specialists. Each division still owns a distinct versioned model identity, checkpoint lineage, benchmark suite, endpoint identity, and release record. Do not claim 65 separately pretrained foundation models.
baseline_requirements: persistent operational database namespace and schema migrations
versioned dataset catalog, object storage, provenance and rights manifests
teacher and student model candidate catalog with pinned revisions and license review
domain-specific ML curriculum and reproducible sandbox labs
authorized reverse-engineering workflow and clean-room specification practice
task, privacy, quality, cost and latency-aware model resource routing
domain benchmarks, protected holdouts, safety and regression evaluation
compute planning, resource metering, run observability and rollback
resource_contract.promotion_rule: A resource becomes connected or certified only after a real integration test and evidence artifact. A catalog candidate, config entry, or successful workflow alone is not proof of availability.

machine_learning_practices: problem framing and measurable success criteria
data validation, deduplication and quality profiling
label design, annotation agreement and inter-rater reliability
train-validation-test split design and leakage prevention
speech recognition, audio understanding and synthesis
RAG, embeddings, reranking and knowledge grounding
SFT, LoRA and QLoRA with rights-cleared data
robustness, adversarial testing, fairness and subgroup analysis
MLOps, reproducibility, model registry and experiment tracking
drift monitoring, scheduled evaluation and retraining gates
privacy, tenant isolation and secure ML supply chain
model serving, autoscaling, latency and cost optimization
model cards, licensing, governance and incident response

database.logical_isolation: One stable division namespace and authorization scope per MasterBot; shared physical infrastructure is permitted.
recommended_stack: PostgreSQL for operational metadata and relational records
pgvector for embeddings where retrieval requires it
PostgreSQL full-text search or dedicated search index for lexical retrieval
SQLite for local sandbox and reproducible offline labs
S3-compatible object storage for immutable datasets, checkpoints and evaluation artifacts
controls: encryption in transit and at rest

source_types: Hugging Face datasets and model cards
customer-contributed opt-in datasets in isolated tenant lanes
synthetic fixtures clearly labeled as synthetic
gates: record source URI, author, revision, retrieval date and content hash
review exact dataset card, file-level license and intended-use terms
verify consent, privacy, personal-data and sensitive-data handling
profile quality, duplicates, schema, language and contamination
create immutable train/validation/test manifests and split hashes
keep benchmark answer keys and private holdouts out of training

orchestrator.role: curriculum, task decomposition, teacher selection and evidence review

teacher_models.candidate_policy: Candidates are catalog references only. Pin exact revision, tokenizer, license, hardware fit, safety profile and benchmark before use.
teacher_models.training_output_policy: Teacher outputs may be used for training or distillation only when the specific model/provider terms and data rights permit it.

reverse_engineering.scope: Only systems, source code, binaries, APIs, UI sessions, workflows and data the operator owns or is explicitly authorized to assess.
workflow: confirm authority, scope and allowed test environment
inventory components, dependencies, interfaces and data flows
observe documented behavior with non-sensitive test inputs
record request/response contracts and state transitions
infer schema and workflow behavior from authorized evidence
write a clean-room specification with citations and unknowns
implement an independently authored alternative in an isolated branch
compare behavior using reproducible tests and security review
prohibited: circumventing DRM or technical protection measures
copying protected code, private datasets, trade secrets or proprietary weights without rights

methods: teacher-generated synthetic data with provenance labels
required_lineage: teacher model ID, exact revision and tokenizer
student base model ID, exact revision and tokenizer
source dataset manifest, license and content hashes
training code, config, seed, hardware and cost
student checkpoint hash and model card
evaluation: compare student against its baseline and teacher on identical tasks
run domain holdouts, general capability, safety and regression tests
measure latency, throughput, memory and cost
reject if quality, privacy or safety regressions exceed approved thresholds
safeguards: never copy teacher weights unless explicit rights permit
never distill from providers whose terms prohibit it
never use customer-private data across tenants
never train on private benchmark holdouts
paid compute and production promotion require separate approval

model_routing.objective: Choose the best eligible model/resource for each task, not simply the largest model.
decision_order: first-party certified model if it meets quality and safety floors
approved local/open-weight candidate with pinned revision
external provider only if configured, permitted, consented and approved
safe fallback or human review when no eligible route exists
signals: reliability, safety and recent error rate
hard_rules: no paid provider use without explicit per-request approval
no external routing of private customer data without explicit consent and policy approval
no training/distillation from model outputs without explicit rights
provider connectors marked contract_only are not considered live

order: free/local CPU evaluation and tiny baselines
available approved local GPU or self-hosted capacity
approved low-cost hosted compute for eligible experiments
larger paid training only after explicit budget approval

suites: latency, throughput, memory and cost benchmark

required: trace IDs across Buddy, model router, jobs and data
release manifest and signed artifact hashes

truth: This map defines resource requirements and candidate references. It does not provision databases, download datasets, connect providers, allocate GPUs, run training, certify teacher models, or prove any division model exists. All unresolved crosswalk mappings remain unassigned until owner approval.
